title: task create swallows a flag-shaped positional title into invalid-arguments with no offending token named
description: Reported by opum-agent 2026-09-18: 'quest task create --title "..."' fails with only 'task create received invalid arguments.', never naming --title as unrecognized. Root cause verified in src/cli/main.ts: task create's title is positional (rest[0], line 2779-2780), not a --title flag. Because rest[0] is captured unconditionally, the literal string '--title' itself becomes the title text, and the value that follows it ('...') is then parsed by flags() as its own argument -- which doesn't start with '--', so flags() returns undefined outright (main.ts:401) rather than reporting an unrecognized flag. usageFailure (main.ts:484-502) can only name a flag when parsed is defined; when parsed is undefined it has nothing to name and falls back to the generic fallback string, exactly the residual gap its own comment documents ('an unparseable argument list ... still gets fallback, since there is no flag to name', main.ts:470-473). So this is the known QCLI-270/QCLI-344 residual gap, hit by a specific and common trigger: a user supplying a flag that does not exist for a command whose first argument is positional.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task create (and any other command with a positional-plus-flags shape) rejects a first positional argument that looks like a flag (starts with --) with a message naming that token, instead of silently treating it as the positional value
quest task create --title "x" (or any nonexistent --flag before a positional command) no longer returns the bare fallback usage sentence with no token named
the fix is verified against the exact repro: quest task create --title "some title" --json

finalSummary:
A new helper, flagShapedPositional (src/cli/main.ts), refuses a first argument that starts with "--" wherever a command takes a positional title or id. The refusal is a usage error, exit 2, naming the token and the usage line, for example: quest task create takes the title as its first argument, but got the flag-shaped "--title". Nothing was run. Usage: quest task create <title> [flags]. It runs right after each group splits its arguments, before any flag parsing, read, or write. That covers task create/view/edit/complete/archive/pause/start/demote, draft create/view/promote/archive, milestone and decision create/view/edit/delete, and milestone archive. --help is intercepted globally before dispatch, so it still resolves. The accepted trade-off is that a title can no longer begin with "--".

VERIFIED:
- AC3, the exact repro: `quest task create --title "some title" --json` now exits 2 with a usage error that contains "--title" and "quest task create <title>". It is no longer the bare fallback, and afterwards `task list` is empty, so nothing was written.
- AC1/AC2: all 21 positional command shapes listed above get exit 2 and a message naming "--bogus". The test asserts its read count is 21. Before the fix, the repro and the 21-shape test both FAILED on "task create received invalid arguments.", and the guard test (a normal title still creates; --help and a flag-only list still exit 0) passed.
- bun run check: 890 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. lore check: 0.
